about: V1 round 1 review judgements (human-style judgement by the validator). Sample drawn by tools/validate/v1_review_sample.py (random.Random(20261106).sample over sorted (model, id) pairs of the 99 spec tasks, n = 25). Evidence: label, REQ statements, finding paraphrases (dump in /tmp/v1r/sample.txt, reproducible with --dump). Verdict ok = label and REQ statements match the finding paraphrases, no invented obligation, actor or deadline.

tasks.message: 'Document monitoring report' sits only in the site-visit branch (GR_SITE, Monitor lane), but REQ-059 and its findings cover every monitoring activity: E6R3 GL:Monitoring Report 'following site and/or centralised monitoring activities' (R1-135), A1-3.11.4.6(a) (R1-067), FDA-RBM23 SQ8 'on-site, remote and centralized' (R4-097). The centralised branch A1-A5 produces no report, yet A11 'Review monitoring reports' follows both branches. Repair: place the report task after the OR join G2 (or add one to the centralised branch) so that both channels feed A11.

tasks.message: 'Submit protocol amendment to FDA' shows the deadline 'subsequently (no period stated) (REQ-085); immediately (REQ-079)'. REQ-079 (21CFR312.30(b)(2)(ii), R4-004, modal may) permits implementing the hazard-eliminating change immediately; it is not a deadline for the FDA submission, which follows 'subsequently' (R4-005). Repair: place REQ-079 on the task that implements the change (L4-03 A1 'Address immediate hazard and its causes' or A2), so A5 keeps only 'subsequently'.

other_findings.message: Binding class without an obligation: these in-scope REQs are binding-law or binding-ICH, but every finding of that class behind them is permissive (modal 'may'), so the elements show LAW/ICH badges for options (instances in the sample: L4-02 A5, L4-03 A5). The classification follows the source class correctly; what is missing is the modal. Repair: keep the binding class but make the permissive nature visible (statement 'may ...', or a 'may' marker carried into the element trace), or downgrade where the option is only good practice. (6 further binding REQs rest only on definition or example findings - REQ-011, 088, 094, 096, 105, 165 - which is acceptable for classification steps.)

The Sponsor sub-process of 'Manage intentional protocol deviations' has two triggers (immediate-hazard deviation report, intentional deviation request) and two unrelated paths that never meet (G1 Yes -> E1; G1 No -> E2/E3). SCP-02 asks for one trigger and one entry point per sub-process; same root cause as the L2 FLW-09 MUST at S1, and G1 only routes on which message arrived (FLW-05 table). Splitting the step (or two start events with an orchestrator-approved exception) resolves both.

Outcome 'No notification required and rationale documented' is reached also when EU CTR does not apply (G2 No) and G6 is No; on that path no task documents a rationale (A4 'Document non-notification rationale', REQ-116 EMA-SB, sits only in the EU serious-breach branch). The named outcome is not true on every path. Repair: name the outcome after what all paths reach (e.g. 'No notification required'), or document the ICH/US non-notification decision (A5 'Assess serious noncompliance' record). The label is the l3_cut outcome (Y1), so align l3_cut.md as well.

notes.md section 6 says A3 'Secure compliance' lies between the deciding task A1 and G1 'Significant noncompliance?', but A2 'Set proportionate remedial actions' (Monitor lane) lies in between as well; the decision is taken three tasks before the gateway. Plausible (the significance is decided when the action is decided), but correct the table or let A3, the task directly before G1, carry the significance assessment (E6R3 A1-3.12.2).

Bare 'CSR' in four labels ('Describe iPDs in CSR section 10.2', 'Describe quality management approach in CSR', 'Report serious breaches in CSR', 'Handle CSR and study data submission') while A11, E1, the model title and L3 use 'clinical study report'; glossary label form is 'clinical study report (CSR)' and D-B1-2 already replaced 'CSR' in L3 E1. Use one form per diagram (e.g. 'clinical study report' throughout, or introduce '(CSR)' once).

Short forms next to the glossary label forms: 'important deviation' / 'non-important deviations' (L4-04 A4, A10, M2; L4-08 A1) vs glossary 'important protocol deviation' (iPD) used in L4-04 G2 and L4-05 M7; 'intentional deviation' (L4-03 A12, E5, M3, M6) vs glossary 'intentional protocol deviation' used in L3 A3, L4-03 title and S2. One term per concept (LBL-04): use the glossary forms (or 'iPD').

'Archive sponsor master file for 25 years' and 'Archive investigator master file for 25 years' use terms that are not in glossary.yaml; EU CTR Art. 58 and the glossary say 'clinical trial master file', and the same model names the records 'Trial master file' (D1) and 'Investigator site file' (D2). Two names for the same records in one diagram (LBL-04/LBL-05). Use the glossary terms, e.g. 'Archive clinical trial master file for 25 years' (sponsor and investigator parts), consistent with D1/D2.

AND split G1 starts A2 'Identify protocol deviations' and A3 'Manage intentional protocol deviations' for every instance, although A3 runs only when an intentional deviation is considered (l3_cut.md). Read literally, the AND join G2 waits for A3 in every trial. Accepted as the orchestrator's reading convention ('channels open in parallel', TA1 on G1, l3_cut.md); listed so that the user confirms the convention for BPMN-literate readers.

passed.check: FLW-05: notes.md section 6 lists all 28 XOR/OR splits with the exact gateway question; every named deciding element exists with the quoted label; every 'directly before' claim holds; deciding element or fixed trial attribute plausible for all 28 (one table inaccuracy, L4-06 G1)

SCP-02: one trigger and named outcomes per sub-process for L4-01, L4-02 (timer start; investigator process is the external participant's own, as l3_cut.md argues), L4-04, L4-06, L4-07, L4-08; exceptions L4-03 S1 and L4-05 E2 reported

LBL-04: no 'protocol violation' in labels (C-17), no bare 'CTR', British spelling 'centralised', CtQ and 'deviation assessment plan' as in the glossary; lanes Sponsor and Monitor from glossary lane_roles; variants reported

not_checked: Fit of the model to the real process (GEN-06): only the process owners can confirm it.

The source documents themselves: the semantic spot check compares task labels and REQ statements with the finding paraphrases (and quotes), not with the source texts; quotes and locators are X1's remit (D4) and were not re-verified offline.
LBL-04 against the source wording of every term: only the project glossary was used as reference.
